subproblem.title: A minimizing current with density invariant along an (n−1)-plane has support in an n-plane (Simon 7.3.3(2), (8)–(10))
subproblem.statement: Assume (CS): Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn S univ) with ∂S = 0, and let L ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with d := dim L < n. Assume the density function of S is invariant under the maps w ↦ y + λw (y ∈ L, λ > 0): whenever HasMassDensity S w θ, also HasMassDensity S (y + λw) θ. Then: (a) S is a cone (IsConeCurrent S); (b) S is invariant under translations by L: S(ω(· + v)) = S(ω), i.e. currentEval (blowUp S (−v) 1) ω = S ω, for v ∈ L and ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P); (c) there is S₀ ∈ 𝒟_{n−d}(ℝ^P) which is minimizing in ℝ^P, has ∂S₀ = 0, is a cone, has spt S₀ ⊆ L^⊥, and satisfies, for all t ∈ L and y ∈ L^⊥: t + y ∈ spt S ⟺ y ∈ spt S₀, and HasMassDensity S (t + y) θ ⟺ HasMassDensity S₀ y θ for every θ ∈ ℝ. (For d ≥ 1, S = [[L]] × S₀.) Assume (ODC): Let P ∈ ℕ and let C ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) be minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ) with ∂C = 0 and C a cone (IsConeCurrent C: η_{0,λ#}C = C for every λ > 0). Then there are e ∈ ℝ^P and m ∈ ℕ such that |e| = 1 whenever m > 0, spt C ⊆ ℝe = span{e}, and Θ^1(μ_C, y) = m (HasMassDensity C y m) for every y ∈ ℝe. (In fact C = m[[ℝe]] up to orientation, or C = 0 with m = 0.) Then for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and every linear subspace L ⊆ ℝ^P with n ≤ P and dim L + 1 = n: if S is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn S univ), ∂S = 0 (BoundaryVanishes S), and HasMassDensity S w θ implies HasMassDensity S (y + λw) θ for all y ∈ L, λ > 0, w ∈ ℝ^P and θ ∈ ℝ, then there is an n-dimensional linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P with spt S ⊆ Q.

Source: parent proof step 4 (exclusion of d = n − 1: 'By the sibling result cone_splitting … spt S ⊆ L + span{e}, a subspace of dimension ≤ n, contained in some n-dimensional subspace Π'''), i.e. Simon 7.3.3, proof of 3.3(2), (8)–(10) (chapter-07.txt lines 556–575: Lemma 3.5 and the form m[[ℓ]] of 1-dimensional minimizing cones). The hypotheses (CS) and (ODC) are the frozen types of the sibling children cone_splitting (Submission.idtp_fons_invariant_cone_splitting) and one_dim_cones (Submission.idtp_fons_one_dim_minimizing_cone); these types are byte-identical to those of the DAG nodes dimred_invariant_cone_splitting and dimred_one_dim_minimizing_cone. The selected node's assembly applies this child to those two siblings and passes the conclusion to the sibling cone_class as its hypothesis (PS).
1. Since dim L + 1 = n, dim L < n. Apply (CS) to (P, n, S, L) with the minimality, ∂S = 0 and invariance hypotheses. It gives S₀ ∈ 𝒟_{n − dim L}(ℝ^P), minimizing in ℝ^P, with ∂S₀ = 0, a cone, spt S₀ ⊆ L^⊥, and, for all t ∈ L and y ∈ L^⊥, t + y ∈ spt S ⟺ y ∈ spt S₀.
2. In ℕ, n − dim L = 1. Transport S₀ along this equality of degrees to S₁ ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) (in Lean: generalize d := n − dim L together with S₀ and substitute d = 1); minimality, BoundaryVanishes, IsConeCurrent and the support are unchanged, so S₁ is minimizing in ℝ^P, ∂S₁ = 0, S₁ is a cone and spt S₁ = spt S₀.
3. Apply (ODC) to S₁: there are e ∈ ℝ^P and m ∈ ℕ with spt S₁ ⊆ span{e}.
4. Let M := L ⊔ span{e}. Then dim M ≤ dim L + dim span{e} ≤ (n − 1) + 1 = n. Let w ∈ spt S. Put t := p_L(w) ∈ L (orthogonal projection L.starProjection, Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem) and y := w − t ∈ L^⊥ (Submodule.sub_starProjection_mem_orthogonal). Then t + y = w ∈ spt S, so y ∈ spt S₀ = spt S₁ ⊆ span{e} (steps 1–3), and w = t + y ∈ M. Hence spt S ⊆ M.
5. Since dim M ≤ n ≤ P = dim ℝ^P, there is a linear subspace Q ⊇ M with dim Q = n: starting from M, as long as the current subspace M' has dim M' < n ≤ P we have M' ≠ ℝ^P, so we may pick v ∉ M' and replace M' by M' ⊔ span{v}, whose dimension is dim M' + 1; after n − dim M steps the dimension is n. Then spt S ⊆ M ⊆ Q, as claimed. ∎
proof_key_steps: cone_splitting with dim L = n − 1 < n gives a 1-dimensional minimizing cone S₀ with t + y ∈ spt S ⟺ y ∈ spt S₀ (t ∈ L, y ∈ L^⊥).
After transporting S₀ to degree 1, one_dim_cones gives spt S₀ ⊆ span{e}.
Orthogonal decomposition w = p_L(w) + (w − p_L(w)) puts spt S inside L ⊔ span{e}, of dimension ≤ n ≤ P, which extends to an n-dimensional Q.

Here the class properties (M1)–(M9) replace the parent's analysis of the currents; the arguments are those of the parent. Uses the reused accepted declaration abstract_dimension_reduction (Submission.abstract_dimension_reduction).
Notation. e₁ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ Euclid 1 (|e₁| = 1); φ_μ(x) := dens μ x • e₁; Hⁿ := μHE[n] = c•μH[n] with c := addHaarScalarFactor(volume, μH[n]) ∈ ℝ≥0, c ≠ 0 (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero); μ^{y,t}, spt, vague convergence as in the statement; q_Q(v) := v − p_Q(v) (|q_Q(v)| ≤ |v|). Fix β > 0. For μ ∈ 𝓜 let R(μ) be the set of w ∈ spt μ for which there are ρ > 0 with B_ρ(w) ⊆ D μ, an n-dimensional Q and s < βρ with |q_Q(y − w)| ≤ s for all y ∈ spt μ ∩ B_ρ(w) ('β-flat points'), and sing'(μ) := ((spt μ ∩ D μ) ∖ R(μ)) ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ D μ).
1. (Measurability of dens μ, any measure μ.) For ρ > 0, x ↦ μ(B_ρ(x)) is lower semicontinuous: if x_j → x then 1_{B_ρ(x)} ≤ liminf_j 1_{B_ρ(x_j)} pointwise, so μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ liminf μ(B_ρ(x_j)) (Fatou). Hence g_ρ(x) := μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) and G_m := sup_{0<ρ<1/(m+1)} g_ρ are lower semicontinuous (suprema of lsc functions), hence Borel. As the intervals (0, 1/(m+1)) form a basis of 𝓝[>]0 and G_m decreases in m, limsup_{ρ→0⁺} g_ρ(x) = inf_m G_m(x) (Filter.HasBasis.limsup_eq_iInf_iSup) is Borel, so dens μ is Borel measurable, and dens μ ≥ 0.
2. (Normalization.) For μ ∈ 𝓜, (M2) and Hⁿ = c•μH[n] give μ = c•(μH[n].withDensity(ofReal ∘ dens μ)). Hence (a) ∫⁻_A ofReal(dens μ) dμH[n] = c^{−1}μ(A) for Borel A; (b) for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), f·dens μ is μH[n]-integrable (by (a) on a ball containing tsupport f and (M1)) and ∫ f·dens μ dμH[n] = c^{−1}∫ f dμ (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul with the measurable ℝ≥0-valued density of step 1); (c) ∫ f·φ_μ dμH[n] = (c^{−1}∫ f dμ)•e₁ (integral_smul_const).
3. (Rescaling, any measure μ, y ∈ ℝ^P, t > 0.) μ^{y,t}(B_ρ(w)) = t^{−n}μ(B_{tρ}(y + tw)) (η_{y,t}^{−1}(B_ρ(w)) = B_{tρ}(y + tw), Measure.map_apply), so the density ratio of μ^{y,t} at (w, ρ) equals that of μ at (y + tw, tρ); since ρ ↦ tρ maps 𝓝[>]0 onto 𝓝[>]0, dens μ^{y,t}(w) = dens μ(y + tw), i.e. φ_{μ^{y,t}}(w) = φ_μ(y + tw); likewise spt μ^{y,t} = {w : y + tw ∈ spt μ}.
4. (The family.) F := {φ_μ : μ ∈ 𝓜} ⊆ (ℝ^P → Euclid 1). Injectivity: if φ_μ = φ_ν (μ, ν ∈ 𝓜) then dens μ = dens ν (e₁ ≠ 0), so μ = ν by (M2). Define sing(φ) := {w : ∃ μ ∈ 𝓜, φ = φ_μ ∧ w ∈ sing'(μ)}; by injectivity sing(φ_μ) = sing'(μ).
5. ((H0), (H1).) If φ_μ = φ_ν μH[n]-a.e., then dens μ = dens ν μH[n]-a.e., hence Hⁿ-a.e. (Hⁿ = c•μH[n]), so μ = ν by (M2) and withDensity_congr_ae, and φ_μ = φ_ν. φ_μ is measurable (step 1) and for every x, ∫_{B_1(x)} |φ_μ| dμH[n] = c^{−1}μ(B_1(x)) < ∞ (step 2(a), (M1) on closedBall x 1); so φ_μ is locally μH[n]-integrable.
6. (A.1.) For φ_μ ∈ F, 0 < λ < 1, |y| ≤ 1 − λ: φ_μ(y + λ·) = φ_{μ^{y,λ}} (step 3) and μ^{y,λ} ∈ 𝓜 (M3).
7. (A.2.) Let φ_μ ∈ F, |y| < 1, and λ_k > 0 strictly decreasing to 0. (M4) gives sub and ν ∈ 𝓜 with dens ν homogeneous and μ^{y,λ_{sub(k)}} → ν vaguely. For k ≥ k₀ (λ_{sub(k)} ≤ 1 − |y| and λ_{sub(k)} < 1), μ^{y,λ_{sub(k)}} ∈ 𝓜 by (M3), so by steps 3 and 2(c), for every f ∈ C_c: ∫ f(x)·φ_μ(y + λ_{sub(k)}x) dμH[n](x) = ∫ f·φ_{μ^{y,λ_{sub(k)}}} dμH[n] = (c^{−1}∫ f dμ^{y,λ_{sub(k)}})•e₁ → (c^{−1}∫ f dν)•e₁ = ∫ f·φ_ν dμH[n] (the finitely many k < k₀ do not affect the limit). ψ := φ_ν ∈ F, and ψ(tx) = ψ(x) for t > 0 by the homogeneity of dens ν.
8. (Support semicontinuity, parent (T3s).) If μ_k, μ ∈ 𝓜, μ_k → μ vaguely, y_k ∈ spt μ_k and y_k → y ∈ D μ, then y ∈ spt μ. Proof: D μ is open (M5), so closedBall y (3ρ₁) ⊆ D μ for some ρ₁ ∈ (0, 1]; by (M6) closedBall y (3ρ₁) ⊆ D μ_k for large k; also |y_k − y| < ρ₁ for large k, so closedBall y_k ρ ⊆ D μ_k for 0 < ρ ≤ ρ₁ and (M7) gives μ_k(B_ρ(y_k)) ≥ e^{−Λρ}ω_nρ^n. Let ε ∈ (0, ρ₁] and take f ∈ C_c with 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, f = 1 on closedBall y (ε/2) and tsupport f ⊆ B_ε(y). For large k, B_{ε/4}(y_k) ⊆ closedBall y (ε/2), so ∫ f dμ_k ≥ μ_k(B_{ε/4}(y_k)) ≥ e^{−Λε/4}ω_n(ε/4)^n. Hence μ(B_ε(y)) ≥ ∫ f dμ = lim ∫ f dμ_k ≥ e^{−Λε/4}ω_n(ε/4)^n > 0 (ω_n > 0); larger ε follow by monotonicity.
9. (A.3, closedness.) spt μ is closed (if μ(B_ε(w)) = 0 then μ(B_{ε/2}(w')) = 0 for w' ∈ B_{ε/2}(w)). R(μ) is relatively open in spt μ: if (ρ, Q, s) witnesses w ∈ R(μ) (s ≥ |q_Q(w − w)| = 0, as w ∈ spt μ ∩ B_ρ(w)), w' ∈ spt μ and t := |w' − w| satisfies (1 + β)t < βρ − s, then (ρ − t, Q, s + t) witnesses w' ∈ R(μ): ρ − t > 0, B_{ρ−t}(w') ⊆ B_ρ(w) ⊆ D μ, and for y ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{ρ−t}(w'), |q_Q(y − w')| ≤ |q_Q(y − w)| + |q_Q(w − w')| ≤ s + t < β(ρ − t). Hence sing'(μ) is closed: if w ∉ sing'(μ) then w ∈ D μ (open) and either w ∉ spt μ — then some ball around w lies in D μ and misses the closed set spt μ, hence misses sing'(μ) — or w ∈ R(μ) — then some ball B around w lies in D μ with B ∩ spt μ ⊆ R(μ), and no point of B is in sing'(μ).
10. (A.3(1).) Let φ_μ = 1_L·c' with dim L = n and c' ∈ Euclid 1. Then dens μ(x) = 0 for x ∉ L and dens μ(x) = a (the coordinate of c') for x ∈ L; in particular dens μ(tx) = dens μ(x) for t > 0 (tx ∈ L ⟺ x ∈ L), so D μ = ℝ^P by (M9). For w ∉ L there is ε > 0 with B_ε(w) ∩ L = ∅ (L is closed), and by (M2) μ(B_ε(w)) = ∫_{B_ε(w)} ofReal(dens μ) dHⁿ = 0; so spt μ ⊆ L. Every w ∈ spt μ lies in R(μ) with (ρ, Q, s) = (1, L, 0): B_1(w) ⊆ ℝ^P = D μ, and for y ∈ spt μ, y − w ∈ L, so q_L(y − w) = 0 and 0 < β. Hence sing(φ_μ) = sing'(μ) = ∅.
11. (A.3(2).) Let φ_μ ∈ F, 0 < λ < 1, |y| ≤ 1 − λ, μ' := μ^{y,λ} ∈ 𝓜 (M3) and g(w) := y + λw. Then φ_μ∘g = φ_{μ'} and spt μ' = g^{−1}(spt μ) (step 3), D μ' = η_{y,λ}(D μ) = g^{−1}(D μ) (M3; η_{y,λ} = g^{−1}), and R(μ') = g^{−1}(R(μ)): (ρ, Q, s) witnesses w ∈ R(μ') iff (λρ, Q, λs) witnesses g(w) ∈ R(μ), since g maps B_ρ(w) onto B_{λρ}(g(w)) and spt μ' ∩ B_ρ(w) onto spt μ ∩ B_{λρ}(g(w)), and q_Q(g(y) − g(w)) = λq_Q(y − w). Hence sing(φ_μ∘g) = sing'(μ') = g^{−1}(sing'(μ)) = g^{−1}(sing φ_μ).
12. (A.3(3).) Let μ, μ_k ∈ 𝓜 with ∫ f·φ_{μ_k} dμH[n] → ∫ f·φ_μ dμH[n] for every f ∈ C_c; by step 2(c) (c ≠ 0, e₁ ≠ 0), μ_k → μ vaguely. Let ε > 0 and suppose that for infinitely many k there is w_k ∈ B_1(0) ∩ sing'(μ_k) with |w_k − z'| ≥ ε for every z' ∈ sing'(μ). Pass to a subsequence along which this holds for every k and w_k → w, |w| ≤ 1 (vague convergence is kept). As B_2(0) ⊆ D μ_k (M5), w_k ∈ spt μ_k ∖ R(μ_k). As closedBall 0 1 ⊆ D μ (M5), step 8 gives w ∈ spt μ; |w − z'| ≥ ε for all z' ∈ sing'(μ), so w ∉ sing'(μ), and hence w ∈ R(μ), witnessed by (ρ, Q, s) with s < βρ. Choose ρ' ∈ (0, ρ) with s < βρ', put τ := (s + βρ')/2 ∈ (s, βρ') and choose η ∈ (0, (ρ − ρ')/2). For large k, |w_k − w| < η, and as closedBall w (ρ' + η) ⊆ B_ρ(w) ⊆ D μ is compact, (M6) gives B_{ρ'}(w_k) ⊆ closedBall w (ρ' + η) ⊆ D μ_k. Claim: for large k, |q_Q(y − w_k)| ≤ τ for every y ∈ spt μ_k ∩ B_{ρ'}(w_k). Otherwise, along a further subsequence there are y_k ∈ spt μ_k ∩ B_{ρ'}(w_k) with |q_Q(y_k − w_k)| > τ; a further subsequence has y_k → y' with |y' − w| ≤ ρ' < ρ, so y' ∈ D μ, step 8 gives y' ∈ spt μ ∩ B_ρ(w), and |q_Q(y' − w)| = lim|q_Q(y_k − w_k)| ≥ τ > s, contradicting the choice of (ρ, Q, s). Hence for large k, (ρ', Q, τ) witnesses w_k ∈ R(μ_k) (τ < βρ'), a contradiction. So there is k₀ with B_1(0) ∩ sing(φ_{μ_k}) ⊆ {x : ∃ z' ∈ sing(φ_μ), |x − z'| < ε} for all k ≥ k₀.
13. (Appendix A.4.) By steps 4–12, abstract_dimension_reduction applies to (P, n, Q := 1, F, sing). Hence either (I) B_1(0) ∩ sing'(μ) = ∅ for every μ ∈ 𝓜, or (II) there is d ∈ ℕ with d + 1 ≤ n such that μH[d + α](sing'(μ) ∩ B_1(0)) = 0 for every μ ∈ 𝓜 and α > 0, and there are ν ∈ 𝓜 and a d-dimensional subspace L with sing'(ν) = L and φ_ν(y + tx) = φ_ν(x) for y ∈ L, t > 0 and all x.
14. (Exclusion of d = n − 1.) Suppose (II) holds with d + 1 = n. Then dens ν(y + tx) = dens ν(x) for y ∈ L, t > 0 (e₁ ≠ 0); in particular (y = 0) dens ν is homogeneous, so D ν = ℝ^P by (M9), and (M8) gives an n-dimensional Q with spt ν ⊆ Q. Every w ∈ spt ν lies in R(ν) with (1, Q, 0) (y − w ∈ Q for y, w ∈ Q), so sing'(ν) = ((spt ν ∩ ℝ^P) ∖ R(ν)) ∪ ∅ = ∅ ≠ L (0 ∈ L): a contradiction. Hence in case (II), d + 2 ≤ n.
15. (Conclusion.) Fix μ ∈ 𝓜 and put Z := sing'(μ) ∩ B_1(0). In case (I), Z = ∅, so μH[s](Z) = 0 for every s. In case (II), d + 2 ≤ n, so n ≥ 2 and, for α > 0, n − 2 + α = d + α' with α' := n − 2 − d + α > 0, whence μH[n − 2 + α](Z) = 0. If n = 1, case (II) is impossible (d + 2 ≤ 1 fails), so Z = ∅. Finally let w ∈ B_1(0) ∩ spt μ with w ∉ Z. Then w ∉ sing'(μ), and as w ∈ B_1(0) ⊆ D μ (M5), w ∈ R(μ): there are ρ > 0 with B_ρ(w) ⊆ D μ, an n-dimensional Q and s < βρ with |(y − w) − p_Q(y − w)| = |q_Q(y − w)| ≤ s for all y ∈ spt μ ∩ B_ρ(w). ∎

subproblem.statement: Assume (DEM), (MON), (DTC) and (PS). Here (DEM) is the frozen statement of Submission.idtp_imrep_measure_density_ae (the registered dependency density_eq_multiplicity_ae of the selected node); (MON) is the frozen type of the sibling child monotonicity (Submission.idtp_fons_minimizing_monotonicity); (DTC) is the contract proposition DensityAndTangentCones (the frozen type of the sibling child tangent_cones, Submission.idtp_fons_density_tangent_cones); (PS) is the conclusion of the sibling child planar_support (Submission.idtp_fons_invariant_planar_support). (DEM): For all P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P and every integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep U n (carrier M, multiplicity θ : ℝ^P → ℕ, orientation ξ), if the measure μ_R := R.measure = θ·μHE[n]⌞M satisfies μ_R(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, then for μHE[n]-almost every x ∈ ℝ^P the ratio μ_R(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) (open balls, ω_n = unitBallVolume n, computed in [0, ∞]) tends to 1_M(x)·θ(x) as ρ ↓ 0. (MON): Let P, n, d ∈ ℕ with 1 ≤ n ≤ d ≤ P, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let N ⊆ ℝ^P be an embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N) with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be minimizing in U ∩ N (IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N)) with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T). Then: (i) for every compact K ⊆ U there is Λ ≥ 0 such that for every y ∈ ℝ^P and R > 0 with closedBall y R ⊆ K the function ρ ↦ e^{Λρ}ρ^{−n}·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) (in [0, ∞], written ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρ^n)·T.massOn (ball y ρ)) is nondecreasing on (0, R); (ii) if N = ℝ^P, then for every y and R with B_R(y) ⊆ U the function ρ ↦ ρ^{−n}·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) is nondecreasing on (0, R); (iii) there is Θ : ℝ^P → ℝ with HasMassDensity T y (Θ(y)) (Θ^n(μ_T, y) = Θ(y)) for every y ∈ U and Θ upper semicontinuous on U; (iv) if y ∈ spt T and HasMassDensity T y θ, then θ ≥ 1. (DTC): Let ℓ ≤ k, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-submanifold with (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N. Then (1) there is Θ: ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ such that Θ^n(μ_T, x) = Θ(x) (limit of M_{B_ρ(x)}(T)/(ω_nρ^n) as ρ ↓ 0, with Θ(x) ≥ 0) for every x ∈ U ∖ spt ∂T, and Θ is upper semicontinuous on U ∖ spt ∂T; (2) for every x ∈ spt T ∖ spt ∂T and every sequence λ_j > 0, λ_j → 0, there are a subsequence λ_{j'} and an integer multiplicity C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+k}), minimizing in ℝ^{n+k}, with η_{x,λ_{j'}#}T ⇀ C in ℝ^{n+k}, μ_{η_{x,λ_{j'}#}T} → μ_C (for all representations), η_{0,λ#}C = C for all λ > 0, and Θ^n(μ_C, 0) = Θ^n(μ_T, x). (PS): For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and every linear subspace L ⊆ ℝ^P with n ≤ P and dim L + 1 = n: if S is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn S univ), ∂S = 0 (BoundaryVanishes S), and HasMassDensity S w θ implies HasMassDensity S (y + λw) θ for all y ∈ L, λ > 0, w ∈ ℝ^P and θ ∈ ℝ, then there is an n-dimensional linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P with spt S ⊆ Q. Under these hypotheses: let n, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≤ k and n ≥ 1, P := n + k, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + ℓ) N) with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T). Let z ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0 with closedBall z (2r) ⊆ U and spt T ∩ B_{2r}(z) ≠ ∅. For a measure μ on ℝ^P and x ∈ ℝ^P let dens μ x := (limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n)).toReal (limsup in [0, ∞] along ρ → 0⁺, ω_n = unitBallVolume n; in the Lean statement dens is a universally quantified function fixed by this defining equation); for y ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, μ^{y,λ} := ofReal(λ^{−n})•μ.map(η_{y,λ}) (= λ^{−n}(η_{y,λ})_#μ, η_{y,λ} = dilation y λ); spt μ := {w : μ(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0}; μ_j → μ vaguely means ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Then there are a set 𝓜 of measures on ℝ^P, a map D from measures on ℝ^P to subsets of ℝ^P, a measure μ₀ and Λ ∈ ℝ such that μ₀ ∈ 𝓜, D(μ₀) = B_2(0), for every w ∈ B_2(0): w ∈ spt μ₀ ⟺ z + rw ∈ spt T, and (M1) every μ ∈ 𝓜 is finite on compact sets; (M2) every μ ∈ 𝓜 equals Hⁿ.withDensity(ofReal ∘ dens μ) (Hⁿ = μHE[n]); (M3) for μ ∈ 𝓜, 0 < λ < 1 and |y| ≤ 1 − λ: μ^{y,λ} ∈ 𝓜 and D(μ^{y,λ}) = η_{y,λ}(D μ); (M4) for μ ∈ 𝓜, |y| < 1 and every strictly decreasing sequence λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0 there are a strictly increasing sub : ℕ → ℕ and ν ∈ 𝓜 with dens ν(tw) = dens ν(w) for all t > 0 and w, and μ^{y,λ_{sub(j)}} → ν vaguely; (M5) for μ ∈ 𝓜, D μ is open and contains B_2(0); (M6) if μ ∈ 𝓜, μ_j ∈ 𝓜 (j ∈ ℕ) and μ_j → μ vaguely, then every compact K ⊆ D μ satisfies K ⊆ D(μ_j) for all large j; (M7) for μ ∈ 𝓜, y ∈ spt μ and ρ > 0 with closedBall y ρ ⊆ D μ: e^{−Λρ}·ω_nρ^n ≤ μ(B_ρ(y)); (M8) if ν ∈ 𝓜 and L is a linear subspace with dim L + 1 = n and dens ν(y + tw) = dens ν(w) for all y ∈ L, t > 0 and w, then spt ν ⊆ Q for some n-dimensional linear subspace Q; (M9) if ν ∈ 𝓜 and dens ν(tw) = dens ν(w) for all t > 0 and w, then D ν = ℝ^P.

Source: parent proof steps 1 and 2 — (a)–(f), density functions (i)–(ix) and (T3s) — and the extremal analysis of step 4; Simon 7.3.3, proof of 3.3(1) (chapter-07.txt lines 454–478: the class 𝒯, (6)–(12)) and proof of 3.3(2) (lines 511–533: (1), (4), (5)), with the parent's departures [D1] (members encoded by their mass measures; the domain is a function D of the measure, recovered from total mass and barycenter) and [D2] (one rescaled ball), and one further departure [D3]. [D3] The zero-scale part of the class is the set of weights of ALL minimizing cycles S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (IsMinimizingIn S univ, ∂S = 0), not only of the weak limits of blow-ups of T at moving centres. Appendix A.4 (consumed by the sibling class_reduction through (M1)–(M9)) needs the class only to be closed under the rescalings of A.1 and to contain the tangent limits of A.2. Tangent limits of positive-scale members are tangent cones of T at points of spt T (DTC (2)) or 0; tangent limits of minimizing cycles of ℝ^P are their tangent cones (DTC (2) with U = N = ℝ^P) or 0; all of these are again minimizing cycles of ℝ^P (step 4(e), step 5). Hence the moving-centre compactness theorem (moving_blowups), the diagonal lemma, the uniform mass bounds and the countable-test criterion of parent step 2(b), (d), (e) are not needed, and neither are moving_blowups nor weak_limit_mass_bound. Every property consumed later, (M1)–(M9), is verified below for this class. Positive-scale members are the rescalings μ_{x,λ} of μ₀ = μ_{T'} (parent (a)). The hypotheses enter as follows: (MON) gives monotonicity and density bounds, (DTC) gives tangent cones, (PS) gives the planar support of (n−1)-invariant members, and (DEM) gives μ = Hⁿ.withDensity(dens μ). The selected node discharges (MON), (DTC) and (PS) with its registered children monotonicity, tangent_cones and planar_support (the last applied to cone_splitting and one_dim_cones), and (DEM) with its registered dependency density_eq_multiplicity_ae. Uses the reused accepted siblings im_mass_measure (Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure), blowup_scaling (Submission.dtc_blowUp_scaling) and cone_measure_homogeneous (Submission.cone_current_imrep_measure_smul_image).
Conventions. P := n + k ≥ 1. η_{a,t} := dilation a t for t > 0, η_{a,t}(v) = t^{−1}(v − a): an affine homeomorphism and measurable embedding with inverse v ↦ a + tv; η_{y,s}∘η_{a,t} = η_{a+ty,ts}; η_{a,t}^{−1}(B_ρ(w)) = B_{tρ}(a + tw); η_{a,t}(B_ρ(v)) = B_{ρ/t}(η_{a,t}(v)); η_{a,t}(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P. For a measure μ, μ^{a,t} := ofReal(t^{−n})•μ.map(η_{a,t}); thus μ^{a,t}(A) = t^{−n}μ(η_{a,t}^{−1}A) for Borel A and (μ^{a,t})^{y,s} = μ^{a+ty,ts} (Measure.map_map, smul). ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞). For A ∈ 𝒟_n(V), η_{a,t#}A := blowUp A a t ∈ 𝒟_n(η_{a,t}(V)). For a current A on an open set V and an IMRep R of A, μ_A := R.measure; by im_mass_measure: (IM-a) M_W(A) = μ_A(W) for open W ⊆ V; (IM-b) for x ∈ V, x ∈ spt A ⟺ μ_A(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0; (IM-c) μ_A does not depend on R. spt μ, dens and vague convergence are as in the statement.
Basic facts. (F1) (Boundaries of blow-ups.) Let V ⊆ ℝ^P, A ∈ 𝒟_n(V) with ∂A = 0 in V (n ≥ 1), a ∈ ℝ^P and t > 0. By the contract's definition, blowUp A a t is the affine push-forward of the restriction of A to η_{a,t}^{−1}(η_{a,t}(V)) = V. The boundary commutes with the affine push-forward (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_affinePushforward) and with restriction of the domain (both sides evaluate A on dω). Hence ∂(η_{a,t#}A) = η_{a,t#}(∂A) = 0, i.e. BoundaryVanishes (η_{a,t#}A). (F2) (blowup_scaling.) Let V be open, A ∈ 𝒟_n(V), a ∈ ℝ^P, t > 0, n ≥ 1. (2) If R represents A, some IMRep R' of η_{a,t#}A has R'.measure = (R.measure)^{a,t} (the Borel-set identity of blowup_scaling (2) and Measure.ext). (3) If A is minimizing in A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P, then η_{a,t#}A is minimizing in η_{a,t}(A₀). (F3) (ℝ^P as a submanifold.) ℝ^P is an embedded C² (n+k)-dimensional submanifold of itself: for every point take V = W = ℝ^P and ψ = id, which is open, C² and injective, with ψ(V) = W ∩ ℝ^P, V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) = K compact for compact K, and Dψ = id injective. Also (closure ℝ^P ∖ ℝ^P) ∩ ℝ^P = ∅. So (MON) and (DTC) apply to a current minimizing in ℝ^P with U = N = ℝ^P, d := n + k, ℓ := k (U ∩ N = ℝ^P, spt ⊆ ℝ^P). (F4) (Vanishing off the support.) If A has open domain V and x ∈ V ∖ spt A, then x lies in the zero region of A (spt A = V ∖ zeroRegion A). So there is ε > 0 with B_ε(x) ⊆ V and μ_A(B_ε(x)) = 0 (IM-b, shrinking ε). Consequently, if t_j > 0 and t_j → 0, then μ_A^{x,t_j}(B_{ε/t_j}(0)) = t_j^{−n}μ_A(B_ε(x)) = 0. So ∫ f dμ_A^{x,t_j} = 0 as soon as tsupport f ⊆ B_{ε/t_j}(0), and ∫ f dμ_A^{x,t_j} → 0 for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). (F5) (Cone weights.) Let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be a cone and R represent C. Then cone_measure_homogeneous gives μ_C(t·A) = t^nμ_C(A) for t > 0 and Borel A. Hence μ_C(B_ρ(tw)) = μ_C(t·B_{ρ/t}(w)) = t^nμ_C(B_{ρ/t}(w)), so the density ratio of μ_C at (tw, ρ) equals the ratio at (w, ρ/t). Since ρ ↦ ρ/t maps 𝓝[>]0 onto 𝓝[>]0, the limsups agree: dens μ_C(tw) = dens μ_C(w). (F6) (Uniqueness of vague limits.) If μ, ν are finite on compact sets and ∫ f dμ = ∫ f dν for all f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), then μ = ν. Proof: let O be open and m ≥ 1; put f_m(x) := min(1, m·infDist(x, Oᶜ))·min(1, (m − |x|)⁺) if O ≠ ℝ^P and f_m(x) := min(1, (m − |x|)⁺) if O = ℝ^P. Each f_m is continuous with support in closedBall 0 m, 0 ≤ f_m ≤ 1_O, and f_m ↑ 1_O pointwise (for x ∈ O, infDist(x, Oᶜ) > 0 since Oᶜ is closed; for x ∉ O, f_m(x) = 0). By monotone convergence, μ(O) = lim_m ∫ f_m dμ = lim_m ∫ f_m dν = ν(O). Open sets form a π-system (isPiSystem_isOpen) generating the Borel σ-algebra (borel α is by definition generateFrom {s | IsOpen s}, and BorelSpace.measurable_eq), and the open balls B_m(0), m ∈ ℕ, are open sets of finite measure covering ℝ^P, so μ = ν (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion). (F7) (Weak limits of blow-ups of cycles are cycles.) Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open, A ∈ 𝒟_n(V) with ∂A = 0 in V, p ∈ V, s_j > 0 with s_j → 0, and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with η_{p,s_j#}A ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly). Then ∂C = 0. Proof: write n = m + 1 and let ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0). Then dω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) and tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω (dω vanishes on the open set where ω vanishes). Choose δ > 0 with B_δ(p) ⊆ V. Then η_{p,s_j}(V) ⊇ η_{p,s_j}(B_δ(p)) = B_{δ/s_j}(0) ⊇ closedBall 0 R for all large j. For such j, ω and dω are test forms on η_{p,s_j}(V), so currentEval(η_{p,s_j#}A, dω) = (η_{p,s_j#}A)(dω) = ∂(η_{p,s_j#}A)(ω) = 0 by (F1). By ConvergesWeakly, C(dω) = lim_j currentEval(η_{p,s_j#}A, dω) = 0, i.e. (∂C)(ω) = 0. Hence ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C). (F8) (The zero current.) The zero current 0 ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) is represented by the IMRep with empty carrier, so it is integer multiplicity with weight 0. It is minimizing in ℝ^P (M_W(0) = 0 ≤ M_W(S') for every competitor S') and ∂0 = 0, and dens 0 ≡ 0. (F9) (Density representation; parent step 2 (iii), Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2) and Theorem 1.9.) 1. Case n = 0. Let R represent T and suppose x₀ ∈ M (H^0 is counting measure, so the a.e. conditions on R hold at every point of M; M is locally finite since ∫_{M∩K}θ dH^0 < ∞). Testing T with a 0-form supported near x₀ shows x₀ ∈ spt T ⊆ N. Let S be represented by (M∖{x₀}, θ, ξ); S is integer multiplicity, SameBoundary holds trivially (n = 0), spt(S−T) = {x₀} ⊆ N ∩ U ∩ W for a small open ball W ⊂⊂ U, and M_W(S) = M_W(T) − θ(x₀) < M_W(T), contradicting minimality. So M = ∅, the first variation vanishes identically, and H := 0 works. Assume n ≥ 1 from now on.
2. Support facts. μ_T(U ∖ spt T) = 0, hence H^n(M ∖ N) = 0. Since N is a C¹ submanifold, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M the approximate tangent space T_xM exists, is the plane oriented by ξ(x) (definition of IMRep) and is contained in T_xN (approximate tangent spaces of subsets of a C¹ submanifold, Ch. 3 §1 and Ch. 2 §4); also div_M X(x) = trace(p_{T_xM}∘DX(x)) = tangentialDivergence (Ch. 4, 2.3).
3. Deformations (book: "φ = φ_t of 2.1 of Ch. 4 with U ∩ N in place of U"; Ch. 4, 2.5–2.6). Let X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^{n+k}) be tangent to N on N ∩ U, K := spt X. X is globally Lipschitz, so it has a C¹ flow φ_t (t ∈ ℝ), each φ_t a C¹ diffeomorphism of U onto U with φ_t = id outside K. N ∩ U is relatively closed in U (because (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅) and X|_{N∩U} is a C¹ tangent field on the C² manifold N; integral curves of this tangent field are integral curves of X, so by uniqueness the orbit of a point of N ∩ U stays in N ∩ U (it cannot leave the relatively closed set N ∩ U while staying in K ∪ {x} ⊂ U). Hence φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U.
4. Competitors (book (2),(3)). Let S_t := φ_{t#}T, defined from the representation (Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.3–3.9): S_t = τ(φ_t(M), θ∘φ_t^{−1}, induced orientation), an integer multiplicity current in U. ∂S_t = 0: choose smooth diffeomorphisms φ^ε of U, equal to the identity outside a fixed compact set, with φ^ε → φ_t in C¹; then φ^ε_#T(dω) = T((φ^ε)^#dω) = T(d(φ^ε)^#ω) = 0 and φ^ε_#T(dω) → S_t(dω) by dominated convergence in the integral formula of 2.24(2). Since φ_t = id off K, spt T ⊆ N and φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U, spt(S_t − T) ⊆ K ∩ N is compact. For any open W with K ⊂ W ⊂⊂ U, minimality gives M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S_t) for all t.
5. First variation (book (1)). By the area formula (Ch. 6, 3.2(3), 3.3–3.5; Ch. 4, 1.7–1.8), M_W(S_t) = ∫_{M∩W} J^M φ_t θ dH^n. Since φ_t(x) = x + tX(x) + o(t) in C¹ uniformly on K, d/dt J^Mφ_t(x)|_{t=0} = div_M X(x) with uniform bounds on K, and θ is integrable on K; so t ↦ M_W(S_t) is differentiable at 0 with derivative ∫_M θ div_M X dH^n (Ch. 4, 2.2). The minimum at t = 0 forces this derivative to vanish: R.firstVariation X = 0. This is IsStationaryAlong N.
6. Mean curvature (Ch. 4, 2.7 and 3.14). Let X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^{n+k}) be arbitrary. Then X^T ∈ C¹_c(U) is tangent to N on N ∩ U, so δV(X^T) = 0 by step 5. On N, X − X^T = X^⊥ is normal to N, and at H^n-a.e. x ∈ M (where T_xM ⊆ T_xN by step 2) div_M X^⊥ = −X·H_N(x), H_N(x) := Σ_{i=1}^n B_x(τ_i, τ_i) with τ_i an orthonormal basis of T_xM and B the second fundamental form of N (Ch. 2, 5.9; Ch. 4, 2.7). Hence δV(X) = −∫ X·H dμ_V with H := H_N on M ∩ N and 0 elsewhere (Borel). On a compact K ⊂ U, K ∩ N is compact (N ∩ U relatively closed), B is continuous, so |H| ≤ √n·sup_{K∩N}|B| μ_V-a.e. on K. This is HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature. (If ℓ = k, B = 0 and H = 0.)

subproblem.title: Simon 7.3.1: densities exist and are upper semicontinuous; blow-up limits at support points are minimizing cones (registered obligation)
subproblem.statement: Let ℓ ≤ k, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-submanifold with (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N. Then (1) there is Θ: ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ such that Θ^n(μ_T, x) = Θ(x) (limit of M_{B_ρ(x)}(T)/(ω_nρ^n) as ρ ↓ 0, with Θ(x) ≥ 0) for every x ∈ U ∖ spt ∂T, and Θ is upper semicontinuous on U ∖ spt ∂T; (2) for every x ∈ spt T ∖ spt ∂T and every sequence λ_j > 0, λ_j → 0, there are a subsequence λ_{j'} and an integer multiplicity C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+k}), minimizing in ℝ^{n+k}, with η_{x,λ_{j'}#}T ⇀ C in ℝ^{n+k}, μ_{η_{x,λ_{j'}#}T} → μ_C (for all representations), η_{0,λ#}C = C for all λ > 0, and Θ^n(μ_C, 0) = Θ^n(μ_T, x).

Source: Simon 7.3.1 and its proof (chapter-07.txt lines 302–364, footnote 2), Remark 2.5(2) (lines 166–174, proof "left to the reader", supplied in step 4), README erratum 3 ((1) on U ∖ spt ∂T, (2) for x ∈ spt T ∖ spt ∂T). For integer multiplicity S, every representation has measure μ_S (Ch. 6, 3.2(3); sibling child im_mass_measure (c)) and M_W(S) = μ_S(W) for open W (sibling child im_mass_measure (a)).
1. Case n = 0: T is minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T ⊆ N, so deleting any point of a representation would give a competitor of smaller mass; hence T = 0, Θ :≡ 0 works and (2) is vacuous. Assume n ≥ 1.
2. Localization. U' := U ∖ spt ∂T is open and T' := T restricted to U' satisfies ∂T' = 0, spt T' ⊆ N, (N̄∖N) ∩ U' = ∅, and T' is minimizing in U' ∩ N: a competitor S' for T' in W ⊂⊂ U' differs from T' by a compactly supported current, so S := T + (S' − T') (extension by zero) is an integer multiplicity competitor for T with the same boundary and the same masses difference on W.
3. Part (1) (book lines 326–328). By the sibling child stationarity (Submission.idtp_fons_minimizing_stationary, frozen type MinimizingImpliesStationary) applied to T' in U', V = v(M, θ) is stationary in N ∩ U', hence (Ch. 4, 2.7) has generalized mean curvature H with |H| ≤ Λ_K := √n·sup_{N∩K}|B_N| on each compact K ⊂ U'. By the monotonicity formula with bounded mean curvature (Ch. 4, 3.17; the book cites 4.7–4.9), for ξ ∈ U' and B_{R}(ξ) ⊂ K: F(ρ)ρ^{−n}μ_T(B_ρ(ξ)) is nondecreasing on (0, R) with F(ρ) ∈ [e^{−Λρ}, e^{Λρ}]. Hence Θ(ξ) := lim_{ρ↓0} μ_T(B_ρ(ξ))/(ω_nρ^n) exists in [0, ∞) for every ξ ∈ U', is upper semicontinuous on U' (Ch. 4, 3.11 argument), and Θ ≥ 1 on spt T ∩ U' (θ ≥ 1 a.e. and Ch. 4, 4.10(1)). Set Θ := 0 off U'. Since M_{B_ρ(ξ)}(T) = μ_T(B_ρ(ξ)) for B_ρ(ξ) ⊂ U, HasMassDensity T ξ (Θ ξ) holds on U' = U ∖ boundarySupport T. (Equivalently, these conclusions — the monotonicity with F(ρ) = e^{Λρ}, existence and upper semicontinuity of Θ on U', and Θ ≥ 1 on spt T ∩ U' — are parts (i), (iii) and (iv) of the sibling child monotonicity (Submission.idtp_fons_minimizing_monotonicity) applied to T' with P := n + k, d := n + ℓ and U := U', whose hypotheses hold by step 2; they transfer to T because M_W(T') = M_W(T) for W ⊆ U' and spt T' = spt T ∩ U'. Either derivation may be used.)
4. Lemma BC (blow-up compactness; Remark 2.5(2) for N_j = η_{x_j,λ_j}(N), "left to the reader", proof supplied). Let x ∈ U', x_j → x, λ_j → 0⁺, S_j := η_{x_j,λ_j#}T. A subsequence satisfies S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^{n+k}, C integer multiplicity, ∂C = 0, C minimizing in ℝ^{n+k}, μ_{S_j} → μ_C. Proof: (i) step 3 gives μ_T(B_ρ(z)) ≤ cρ^n near x, so M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) ≤ cR^n and ∂S_j = 0 on B_{r/λ_j}(0) for large j; (ii) Ch. 6, 2.15 (diagonal in R) and 3.11 give a weak limit C (every test form is eventually supported in η_{x_j,λ_j}(U), where currentEval equals S_j) with ∂C = 0, integer multiplicity; (iii) if dist(x_j,N)/λ_j is unbounded, then along a subsequence it tends to ∞, every ball B_R(0) eventually misses η_{x_j,λ_j}(N) ⊇ spt S_j, so C = 0 and μ_{S_j} → 0; otherwise dist(x_j, N) ≤ C₀λ_j for all j and some C₀ < ∞, x ∈ N and, with π the nearest point projection onto N (C¹ near x, π = id on N, Lip(π|B_s(z)) ≤ 1 + cs), the retractions π_j := η_{x_j,λ_j}∘π∘η_{x_j,λ_j}^{−1} onto η_{x_j,λ_j}(N) have Lipschitz constants L_j → 1 on each ball; (iv) run the proof of 2.4: for compact K, a cut-off ψ and W_s := {ψ > s}, Ch. 6, 7.2 gives C − S_j = ∂R_j + S'_j with masses in W_0 → 0, slicing (Ch. 6, 4.5) at a good α gives C⌞W_α = S_j⌞W_α + ∂R̃_j + S̃_j with M(R̃_j) + M(S̃_j) → 0 and boundary error P_j on {ψ = α}, M(P_j) → 0; fix G > 0 with spt ψ ∪ π_j(spt ψ) ⊆ B_G(0) for all large j (|π_j(z) − z| = dist(z, η_{x_j,λ_j}(N)) ≤ |z| + C₀, C₀ as in (iii)); for an integer multiplicity cycle X with spt X ⊆ K put Y_j := X + ∂R̃_j and Z_j := S_j + π_{j#}Y_j (π_{j#} is applied only to the compactly supported Y_j; Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.9): ∂Z_j = ∂S_j (as ∂π_{j#}Y_j = π_{j#}∂Y_j = 0) and spt(Z_j − S_j) ⊆ π_j(spt Y_j) ⊆ η_{x_j,λ_j}(N) ∩ B_G(0), so Z_j is a competitor for S_j in η_{x_j,λ_j}(U ∩ N) (dilations preserve minimality); since π_j is C¹ and equals the identity on spt S_j, the push-forward formula (Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.3–3.9) gives π_{j#}(S_j⌞B_G(0)) = S_j⌞B_G(0), so Z_j⌞B_G(0) = π_{j#}((S_j + Y_j)⌞B_G(0)) and μ_{S_j}(B_G) ≤ μ_{Z_j}(B_G) ≤ L_j^nμ_{S_j+Y_j}(B_G); comparing off {ψ ≥ α} as in 2.4 (book (9)–(11)), M_{W_α}(S_j) ≤ M_{W_α}(C+X) + M(S̃_j) + M(P_j) + (L_j^n − 1)Λ_G with Λ_G := sup_j μ_{S_j+Y_j}(B_G(0)) ≤ cG^n + M(X) + sup_j M(∂R̃_j) < ∞ (∂R̃_j = (C − S_j)⌞W_α − S̃_j); (v) lower semicontinuity gives M_{W_α}(C) ≤ M_{W_α}(C+X), hence C is minimizing in ℝ^{n+k} (localize to an arbitrary W ⊂⊂ ℝ^{n+k} as in 2.4), and with X = 0, limsup μ_{S_j}(K) ≤ μ_C(K); with lower semicontinuity on open sets and the layer-cake formula, μ_{S_j} → μ_C (for every sub-subsequence, hence for the subsequence). [This replaces footnote 2: competitors are arbitrary in ℝ^{n+k}, so no projection onto T_xN is needed.]
5. Part (2) (book (1)–(4)). Let x ∈ spt T ∖ spt ∂T and apply Lemma BC with x_j = x: S_{j'} ⇀ C, C minimizing, μ_{S_{j'}} → μ_C. For each ρ > 0, (ω_nρ^n)^{−1}μ_{S_j}(B_ρ(0)) = (ω_n(λ_jρ)^n)^{−1}μ_T(B_{λ_jρ}(x)) → Θ(x) (book (1)). For all but countably many ρ, μ_C(∂B_ρ(0)) = 0, so μ_{S_{j'}}(B_ρ(0)) → μ_C(B_ρ(0)) (book (4)); by monotonicity in ρ and left-continuity, μ_C(B_ρ(0)) = ω_nρ^nΘ(x) for all ρ > 0. Hence HasMassDensity C 0 Θ(x) and HasMassDensity T x Θ(x).
6. Cone property (book lines 342–360). By the sibling child stationarity (ℓ = k, U = N = ℝ^{n+k}), V_C is stationary in ℝ^{n+k}. Since ρ^{−n}μ_C(B_ρ(0)) is constant, the monotonicity identity (Ch. 4, 3.6) gives D^⊥r = 0 μ_C-a.e., i.e. x ∈ T_xV_C, so x ∧ C⃗(x) = 0 μ_C-a.e.; Lemma 2.33 of Ch. 6 (homotopy formula, ∂C = 0, locally finite mass) gives η_{0,λ#}C = C for all λ > 0. As dilation 0 λ '' ℝ^{n+k} = ℝ^{n+k}, currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = C(η_{0,λ}^#ω) = C(ω): IsConeCurrent C.
7. Output: the subsequence (strictly increasing), C, ConvergesWeakly and MassMeasuresConverge from step 5 and Lemma BC (all representations have the measures μ_{S_j}, μ_C), IsMinimizingIn C univ, IsConeCurrent C, and θ = Θ(x).
proof_key_steps: Localize to U∖spt ∂T; stationarity and bounded mean curvature give monotonicity, existence and upper semicontinuity of Θ.
Blow-up compactness with retractions onto η(N): limits are minimizing with mass convergence.
Constant density ratios of the limit give x ∈ T_xV_C a.e., so C is a cone with Θ(C,0) = Θ(T,x).
